title: Alternating with Sharkey at the Famous Door
summary: He led the commercial band at the Famous Door, ordered to play everything but Dixieland.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well this is the band that was playing at the famous door with him.
Yeah, that's it. And you were alternating around that time, huh?
Yeah. I had, as I said, the commercial band. My job was to play just anything that wasn't Dixieland, just the opposite.
Well who was there with you at the famous door?

I had George Hartman played bass and trumpet doubled, and Roger Johnson, who was deceased, played drums, and Charlie Hewitt played piano. And Jackie Blaine sang, and the boy was Billy McCree, Irish tenor. And we had to play everything that Schalke didn't play, just the opposite. That was my orders, don't play Andy Dixieland. Don't encroach on Schalke's territory.
